title: Surprise holiday ideas: how to plan a mystery trip
intro: A surprise holiday turns the trip into an adventure before it even starts. Here's how to plan one, keep the secret and reveal it in a way nobody will forget.
seo_title: Surprise holiday ideas: how to plan a mystery trip

sections.heading: Why plan a surprise holiday?
sections.text:
Not knowing where you're going is half the fun. The build-up becomes part of the holiday, and there's no arguing about where to go, because nobody knows. A surprise trip also gets you somewhere you'd never have picked, which is often where the best memories come from.

It suits lots of occasions: a birthday or anniversary, a reward after exams, a treat for children who've been asking "where are we going?" for months, or just a way to make an ordinary half term feel special.

sections.heading: Find out what they'd love, without asking
sections.text:
The risk with a surprise is that it's somewhere the other person doesn't want to go. So do some quiet research first. What did they love about past trips? Have they mentioned somewhere they've always wanted to see? Do they hate the heat, long flights or early starts?

Play it safe on the big things (temperature, travel time, how busy it is) and save the surprise for the place itself. A short flight somewhere warm, like [Madeira](/destinations/madeira) or [Malta](/destinations/malta), is easier to get right than a long-haul trip.

sections.heading: Keep it a secret
sections.text:
- **Book in your own name** and switch off email notifications on shared devices.
- **Tell them only what they need:** the dates, roughly what to pack, and whether they need a passport.
- **Give a packing list,** not a destination. "Swimming things, one warm jumper, comfortable shoes" keeps the mystery while making sure nobody arrives in the wrong clothes.
- **Take care at the airport.** Departure boards give the game away, so decide whether the airport itself is the reveal.

sections.heading: Make the reveal part of the fun
sections.text:
How you reveal it is the moment everyone will remember. A few ideas:
- **Clues in the run-up.** One clue a day for a week, from the weather to a food or a word in the local language.
- **A homemade boarding pass** in an envelope, opened on the morning you leave.
- **A suitcase with a hint inside,** like a phrasebook or a guidebook.
- **At the airport,** let them find the flight on the departures board themselves.
- **A scratch card or a map with a pin,** revealed bit by bit.

sections.heading: Let the draw keep it a surprise for everyone
sections.text:
There's another way to make a holiday a surprise: let everyone choose, but leave the final pick to chance. In somewhere🎉, each person adds the places they'd love to go and spreads points in secret. Nobody sees anyone else's points, and nobody knows which place will win until the departures board reveals it.

So the whole family gets a say, and the result is still a surprise, even for the person who organised it. Read [how the draw works](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday) in our guide to deciding where to go.

sections.heading: A few surprise holiday ideas
sections.text:
Not sure where to send them? Some places that make a great surprise:
- **A first look at snow:** [Rovaniemi](/destinations/rovaniemi) or [Tromsø](/destinations/tromso) in winter
- **A warm escape in winter:** [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) or [Cape Verde](/destinations/cape-verde)
- **A city that feels like a film set:** [Prague](/destinations/prague), [Vienna](/destinations/vienna) or [Kotor](/destinations/kotor)
- **A once-in-a-lifetime trip:** [Tokyo](/destinations/tokyo), [the Maldives](/destinations/maldives) or a safari in the [Maasai Mara](/destinations/maasai-mara)

Or browse [where to go in each month](/destinations/where-to-go-in-december) for something at its best when you travel.

faqs.question: How do you plan a surprise holiday?
faqs.answer: Find out what they'd enjoy without asking directly, book in your own name, tell them only the dates and what to pack, and plan a fun reveal, such as clues in the run-up or a homemade boarding pass.

faqs.question: How do you reveal a surprise holiday?
faqs.answer: Popular ways are a clue a day in the week before, a homemade boarding pass in an envelope, a suitcase with a phrasebook inside, or letting them find the flight on the departures board at the airport.

faqs.question: Can the whole family choose and still have a surprise?
faqs.answer: Yes. Let everyone add ideas and spread points in secret, then let a draw pick the winner. Nobody knows which place will win until the draw, not even whoever set it up.
